question.text: Lease liability on a balance sheet arises when:

answer.text: A company owns an asset outright
A company acquires the right to use an asset under a lease agreement for more than one year
A company writes off bad debts

explanation.text: The Logic: When a company leases an asset for more than one year, it recognizes a lease liability representing the fair value of lease minus amounts repaid. Analysts often treat this as part of debt. The Trap: Ownership means PPE (not lease). Selling creates a gain/loss. Bad debts are provisions, not lease liabilities. Cross-Exam Context: Lease accounting tested in NISM XV Ch 8.
